89.h: 85 - Reports Concerning al-Najāshī, King of Abyssinia *
89.t:
His name: Aṣḥamah, king of Abyssinia, counted among the Companions (الصحابي) (may Allah be pleased with them).
He was among those whose (4) Islam was good; he did not emigrate and had no sighting of him, so he is a Successor (التابعي) in one respect and a Companion (الصحابي) in another.
He died during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ, and he prayed over him with the people the prayer over the absent (5) , ⟦1:428⟧ and it is not established that he ﷺ prayed over any absent person other than him.
The reason for that: he died among a Christian people, and there was no one with him to pray over him, because the Companions (الصحابي) who had been emigrants with him had left him, emigrating to Medina in the year of Khaybar.
Ibn Isḥāq, from al-Zuhrī, who said:
I narrated to ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr the hadith of Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān from Umm Salamah about the story of al-Najāshī and his words to ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ:
By Allah, Allah did not take a bribe from me when He restored my kingdom to me, and He did not obey people concerning me, so that I should obey people concerning Him.
ʿUrwah said: Do you know what it means?
I said: No.
He said: ʿĀʾishah narrated to me that his father was the king of his people, and he had no son except al-Najāshī. Al-Najāshī had an uncle who had twelve sons of his own loins, and they were the household of the kingdom of Abyssinia.
The Abyssinians said among themselves: If we kill al-Najāshī's father and make his brother king, for he has no son other than this boy, while his brother has twelve sons, they will inherit his kingdom after him, and Abyssinia will remain after him for a long time.
So they fell upon al-Najāshī's father and killed him, and made his brother king, and they remained thus. Al-Najāshī grew up with his uncle; he was an intelligent and resolute man, and he gained mastery over his uncle's affairs and attained every station with him.
When the Abyssinians saw his standing with him, they said among themselves:
By Allah, we fear that he will make him king, and if he makes him king over us he will kill us all; he knows well that it was we who killed his father. So they went to ⟦1:429⟧ his uncle and said to him:
Either kill this young man or expel him from our midst, for we fear for ourselves from him.
He said: Woe to you! You killed his father yesterday, and shall I kill him today? Rather, expel him from your land.
So they took him out and sold him to a merchant for six hundred dirhams, who then put him on a ship and set off with him. Then, when it was the evening of that day, a cloud of the autumn clouds rose up, and his uncle went out to seek rain beneath it; a thunderbolt struck him and killed him.
The Abyssinians turned in alarm to his sons, but they were fools, with no good in any of his sons, and the affair of the Abyssinians fell into disorder. When their situation became too hard for them, they said to one another:
You know, by Allah, that your king, the only one who can set your affairs right, is the one you sold this morning. If you have any concern for the affair of Abyssinia, then catch up with him.
He said: So they went out in search of him until they caught up with him, took him from the merchant, then brought him back, placed the crown on him, seated him on the royal throne and made him king. Then the merchant came to them and said:
Either give me my money, or I will speak to him about it.
They said: We will not give you anything.
He said: Then, by Allah, I will speak to him.
They said: Go ahead.
So he came to him, sat before him, and said:
O king! I bought a boy from some people in the market for six hundred dirhams; they handed him over to me and took my dirhams, but when I had set off with my boy they caught up with me, took my boy and withheld my dirhams from me.
al-Najāshī said to them: You shall give him his dirhams, or he shall place his boy in his hands, and he shall take him wherever he wishes.
They said: Rather, we will give him his dirhams.
She said: That is why he says: Allah did not take a bribe from me when He restored my kingdom to me, so that I should take a bribe concerning it. That was the first thing known of his firmness in his religion and his justice in his judgement.
Then she said: When al-Najāshī died, we used to say among ourselves that a light was continually seen over his grave (1) .
The Musnad of Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal: حدثنا يعقوب بن إبراهيم، حدثنا أبي، عن ابن إسحاق، حدثني ابن شهاب، عن أبي بكر بن عبد الرحمن بن الحارث بن ⟦1:430⟧ هشام، عن أم سلمة زوج النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قالت: 
When we alighted in the land of Abyssinia, we lived there beside the best of neighbours, al-Najāshī. He made us secure in our religion, and we worshipped Allah the Exalted without being harmed and without hearing anything we disliked.
When that reached Quraysh, they resolved to send to al-Najāshī concerning us (1) two tough men, and to give al-Najāshī gifts of what was prized among the goods of Mecca; among the things from it that pleased him most was leather.
So they gathered a great deal of leather for him, and they did not leave a single one of his patricians without giving him a gift. Then they sent that with ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Rabīʿah ibn al-Mughīrah al-Makhzūmī and ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ al-Sahmī, instructed them in their plan, and said to them:
Give each patrician his gift before you speak to al-Najāshī about them, then present him with his gifts, then ask him to hand them over to you before he speaks to them.
She said: So the two set out and came to al-Najāshī, while we were with him in the best abode, with the best neighbour. Not one of his patricians remained but they gave him his gift, and they said to him:
Some foolish young men of ours have taken refuge (2) in the king's country. They have abandoned the religion of their people and have not entered your religion, and they have brought an invented religion that neither we nor you know. The nobles of their people have sent us to the king concerning them, so that he may return them to them. So when we speak to the king about them, advise him to hand them over to us and not to speak to them, for their people have the keenest eye on them (3) , and know best what they have reproached them for.
They said to them: Yes.
Then the two presented al-Najāshī's gifts, and he accepted them from them; then they spoke to him and said to him:
O king! Some foolish young men of ours have taken refuge in your country. They have abandoned the religion of their people and have not entered your religion, and they have brought an invented religion that neither we nor you know. The nobles of their people, from their fathers, their uncles and their clans, have sent us to you so that you may return them to them, for they have the keenest eye on them, and know best what they have reproached ⟦1:431⟧ them for.
She said: Nothing was more hateful to ʿAbd Allāh and ʿAmr than that al-Najāshī should hear their words.
His patricians around him said: They have spoken the truth, O king, so hand them over to the two of them.
al-Najāshī became angry, then said: No, by Allah! In that case I will not hand them over to the two of them, nor will I be plotted against (1) concerning a people who have sought my protection, settled in my land and chosen me over others, until I summon them and question them.
Then he sent for the Companions of the Messenger of Allah and summoned them. When his messenger came to them they gathered, then some of them said to others:
What will you say to the man when you come to him?
They said: We will say, by Allah, what we know and what our Prophet ﷺ commanded us, whatever may come of it.
When they came to him, al-Najāshī having summoned his bishops, who spread out their scriptures around him, he questioned them, saying:
What is this religion for which you have parted from your people, without entering my religion or the religion of any of these nations?
She said: The one who spoke to him was Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib, and he said to him:
O king! We were a people of the Jāhiliyyah (الجاهلية): we worshipped idols, ate carrion, committed obscenities, severed ties of kinship and treated our neighbours badly, and the strong among us devoured the weak. We remained (2) thus until Allah sent us a messenger from among ourselves, whose lineage, truthfulness, trustworthiness and chastity we knew. He called us to Allah, to affirm His oneness and worship Him, and to cast off the stones and idols that we and our fathers used to worship besides Him. He commanded us to speak the truth, to fulfil trusts, to maintain ties of kinship, to be good neighbours, and to refrain from forbidden things and bloodshed. He forbade us obscenities, false speech, consuming the wealth of the orphan and slandering chaste women. He commanded us to worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and commanded us to pray, to give zakat and to fast.
She said: He enumerated to him the matters of Islam.
We believed him, had faith in him and followed him. Then our people attacked us, tortured us (3) , and tried to turn us from our religion to bring us back to the worship of idols, and to make us regard as lawful the foul things we used ⟦1:432⟧ to regard as lawful. When they overpowered us, wronged us, oppressed (1) us and came between us and our religion, we went out to your country, chose you over others, desired your protection, and hoped that we would not be wronged with you, O king.
She said: He said: Do you have with you anything of what he brought from Allah?
He said: Yes.
He said: Then recite it to me.
So he recited to him the opening of: “Kāf Hā Yā ʿAyn Ṣād” (Qurʾān 19:1) , and al-Najāshī wept, by Allah, until his beard was wet, and his bishops wept until they wet their scriptures when they heard what was recited to them.
Then al-Najāshī said: This and what Moses brought come forth from a single lamp-niche. Go, both of you; by Allah, I will never hand them over to you, nor will I be plotted against.
When the two had gone out, ʿAmr said: By Allah, tomorrow I will tell him their fault, then (2) I will root them out completely.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Rabīʿah, who was the more God-fearing of the two men towards us, said to him:
Do not do it, for they are our kin, even though they have opposed us.
He said: By Allah, I will tell him that they claim that Jesus is a servant.
Then he went to him the next morning and said: O king! They say a grave thing about Jesus son of Mary, so send for them and ask them what they say about him.
So he sent to ask them.
She said: Nothing like it had befallen us. The people gathered, then said:
We will say about him, by Allah, what Allah the Exalted said, whatever may come of it.
When they entered upon him, he said to them: What do you say about Jesus?
Jaʿfar said to him: We say about him what our Prophet (3) brought: he is the servant of Allah, His messenger, His spirit and His word, which He cast into Mary, the chaste virgin.
al-Najāshī struck his hand on the ground, took up a stick, then said:
Jesus does not go beyond what you have said by so much as this stick.
His patricians around him snorted, ⟦1:433⟧ and he said: Even if you snort, by Allah! Go, for you are suyūm in my land (al-suyūm: those who are safe). Whoever reviles you will be fined, and again whoever reviles you will be fined. I would not love to have a dabrā (1) of gold and to have harmed a single man among you (al-dabr in their language: the mountain). Return their gifts to the two of them, for by Allah, Allah did not take a bribe from me when He restored my kingdom to me, so that I should take a bribe concerning it, and He did not obey people concerning me, so that I should obey them concerning Him.
The two went out disgraced, with what they had brought returned to them, and we stayed with him in the best abode with the best neighbour.
By Allah, we were in that state when someone came against him (meaning: one contesting his kingdom), and by Allah, we never knew any distress more severe than the distress that befell us (2) , for fear that that man would prevail over al-Najāshī and a man would come who did not know of our rights what al-Najāshī knew.
al-Najāshī marched out, and between the two of them lay the breadth of the Nile.
The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Who will go out to witness the battle of the people, then bring us the news?
al-Zubayr said: I will.
He was among the youngest of the people in age. They inflated a waterskin for him, which he placed under his chest, then swam on it until he came out at the place where they met, and witnessed it.
We prayed to Allah for al-Najāshī to be victorious over his enemy and to be established in his land, and the affair of Abyssinia was consolidated (3) for him. We remained with him in the best of abodes until we came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was in Mecca (4) .
سليمان ابن بنت شرحبيل: عن عبد الرحمن بن بشير، وعبد الملك بن ⟦1:434⟧ هشام، عن زياد البكالي، وأحمد بن محمد بن أيوب، عن إبراهيم بن سعد جميعا:
عن ابن إسحاق، عن الزهري، عن أبي بكر بن عبد الرحمن، عن أم سلمة، عن جعفر بن أبي طالب:
that al-Najāshī asked him: What is your religion?
He said: Allah sent among us a messenger ... , and he mentioned some of what has preceded.
Ibn Isḥāq is alone in narrating it as connected.
As for (1) ʿUqayl, Yūnus and others, they narrated it as mursal (مرسل).
Ibn Idrīs narrated it from Ibn Isḥāq, and said:
عن الزهري، عن أبي بكر بن عبد الرحمن، وعروة، وعبيد الله، عن أم سلمة.
This report is also narrated from Abū Burdah ibn Abī Mūsā, from his father, and from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib, from his father (2) .
ورواه: ابن شابور، عن عثمان بن عطاء، عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس at full length.
aʿlā bihim ʿaynan: more perceptive of them.
lā hā Allāh: an oath. The scholars of Arabic say: lā hā Allāh dhā, and the hā replaces the wāw of the oath, that is: no, by Allah, this shall not be.
It has also been said: rather, the wāw of the oath was dropped and hā was separated from hādhā, so the divine name came in between, and it was put in the accusative (3) because of the dropping of the wāw of the oath.
tanākharat: al-nakhīr is a sound from the nose.
It has also been said: al-nakhīr is a kind (4) of speech.
In one narration it came as: than a grief with which we grieved.
Her words “until we came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Mecca”: she meant herself and her husband.
Likewise al-Zubayr, Ibn Masʿūd and a group of the emigrants to Abyssinia came to Mecca, having grown weary of living in Abyssinia.
Then a group came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when they learned that he had emigrated to ⟦1:435⟧ Medina, then Jaʿfar came with those who remained, in the days of Khaybar.
Abū Mūsā al-Aṣbahānī the hadith master (الحافظ) said: The name of al-Najāshī is Aṣḥamah.
It has also been said: Aṣḥam ibn Bujrā.
He had a son named Armā, whom he sent to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he died on the way.
It has also been said that the one who accompanied ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ was ʿUmārah ibn al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah al-Makhzūmī.
Abū Kurayb and Muḥammad ibn Ādam (1) al-Maṣṣīṣī said:
حدثنا أسد بن عمرو، حدثنا مجالد (2) ، عن الشعبي، عن عبد الله بن جعفر، عن أبيه، قال: 
Quraysh sent ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ and ʿUmārah ibn al-Walīd with a gift from Abū Sufyān to al-Najāshī.
They said to him, while we were with him: Some of our lowly and foolish people have come to you, so hand them over to us.
He said: No, not until I hear what they say ... , and he mentioned something similar.
Until he said: He ordered a crier, who called out:
Whoever harms any one of them, fine him four dirhams.
Then he said: Is that enough for you?
We said: No.
So he doubled it.
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ emigrated to Medina and prevailed there, we said to him:
Our companion has gone out to Medina and emigrated, and has killed (3) those we had told you about. We wish to depart to him, so provide for us.
He said: Yes.
So he gave us mounts, provisions and gifts, then said:
Inform your companion of what I have done for you. This is my messenger with you. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that he is the Messenger of Allah, so tell him to ask forgiveness for me.
Jaʿfar said: We went out until we reached Medina, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ met me and embraced me (4) , ⟦1:436⟧ and said: (I do not know whether I am happier at the conquest of Khaybar or at the arrival of Jaʿfar) .
Then he sat down, and al-Najāshī's messenger stood up and said:
This is Jaʿfar; ask him what our master did for him.
I said: Yes -meaning: I mentioned it to him-.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up, performed ablution, then prayed three times: (O Allah, forgive al-Najāshī) .
The Muslims said: Āmīn.
I said to the messenger: Go, and tell your master what you have seen (1) .
ابن أبي عدي، ومعاذ: عن ابن عون (2) ، عن عمير بن إسحاق:
that Jaʿfar said: O Messenger of Allah! Give me leave to go to a land where I can worship Allah.
He gave him leave, and he came to al-Najāshī.
ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ narrated to us; he said:
When I saw Jaʿfar living there in safety, he and his companions, I envied him, so I came to al-Najāshī and said:
In your land there is a man whose cousin is in our land, who claims that people have only one god. If you do not kill him and his companions, I will never cross this water to you again, nor will any of my companions.
He said: Go to him and summon him.
I said: He will not come with me, so send a messenger with me.
We came to him while he was among his companions, talking to them.
He said to him: Respond.
When we reached the door, I called out: Give leave to ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ.
Jaʿfar called out: Give leave to the party of Allah.
He heard his voice and gave him leave before me ... , the hadith (3) .
إسرائيل: عن أبي إسحاق، عن أبي بردة، عن أبيه، قال: 
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to set off with Jaʿfar to the land of al-Najāshī. That reached Quraysh, so they sent ʿAmr and ʿUmārah ibn al-Walīd, and gathered a gift for al-Najāshī.
The two came to him and brought him the gift, ⟦1:437⟧ and he accepted it, and they prostrated to him.
Then ʿAmr said: Some people of our land have turned away from our religion, and they are in your land.
He said: In my land?
He said: Yes.
He sent for us, and Jaʿfar said to us:
None of you is to speak; I am your spokesman today.
We reached al-Najāshī while he was sitting in a great assembly, with ʿAmr on his right and ʿUmārah on his left, and the priests and monks sitting in two rows.
ʿAmr had said to him: They do not prostrate to you.
When we arrived, those with him hastened to tell us: Prostrate!
We said: We prostrate only to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
When we came up to al-Najāshī, he said: What prevented you from prostrating?
He said: We prostrate only to Allah.
He said: And why is that?
He said: Allah sent among us a messenger, and he is the one whose coming Jesus foretold, saying: “who will come after me, whose name is Aḥmad” (Qurʾān 61:6) . He commanded us to worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, to establish prayer and to give zakat; he commanded us what is right and forbade us what is wrong.
His words pleased al-Najāshī.
When ʿAmr saw that, he said: May Allah set the king right, they differ from you concerning the son of Mary.
al-Najāshī said to Jaʿfar: What does your companion say about the son of Mary?
He said: He says about him the word of Allah: he is the spirit of Allah and His word, whom He brought forth from the chaste virgin whom no man had approached and whom no child had opened (1) .
He took up a stick, raised it, and said:
O company of priests and monks! What they say does not exceed what you say about the son of Mary by the weight of this. Welcome to you and to the one from whom you have come. I bear witness that he is the Messenger of Allah, and that he is the one whose coming Jesus foretold. Were it not for the kingship I am in, I would go to him so that ⟦1:438⟧ I might kiss his sandal. Stay in my land as long as you wish.
He ordered food and clothing for us, and said: Return their gift to these two.
ʿAmr was a short (1) man, and ʿUmārah was a handsome man. The two had come by sea to al-Najāshī, and he drank with ʿAmr and his wife.
When they had drunk wine, ʿUmārah said to ʿAmr: Tell your wife to kiss me.
He said: Are you not ashamed?
ʿUmārah seized ʿAmr to throw him into the sea, and ʿAmr kept imploring him until he let him go.
ʿAmr bore a grudge against him, and said to al-Najāshī: When you go out, ʿUmārah takes your place with your household.
So he summoned ʿUmārah, and something was blown into his urethra, and he flew off with the wild beasts (2) .
From Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah, from Ibn Shihāb, who said:
ʿAmr plotted against ʿUmārah and said: O ʿUmārah! You are a handsome man, so go to al-Najāshī's wife and converse with her when her husband goes out, for that will help us in our purpose.
ʿUmārah sent messages to her until he went in to her.
ʿAmr went to al-Najāshī and said: My companion is a womaniser, and he desires your wife.
al-Najāshī sent to his house, and there he was with his wife. He gave orders concerning him, and his sorcerers blew into his urethra; then he cast him onto one of the islands of the sea, and he went mad and lived wild with the wild beasts.
ابن إسحاق: عن يزيد بن رومان، عن عروة (3) ، عن عائشة، قالت: 
When ⟦1:439⟧ al-Najāshī died, we used to say among ourselves that a light was continually seen over his grave (1) .
As for ʿUmārah, he remained with the wild beasts until the caliphate (الخلافة) of ʿUmar. His brother was shown where he was, so he went to him and waited for the time when he came down to the water. When he saw his brother he fled, but he leapt upon him and seized him, and he kept crying out:
Let me go, O my brother!
But he did not let him go, and his strength gave way from fear, and he died on the spot.
So he is counted among the madmen who will be resurrected in the state they were in before losing their reason; this wretch (2) will be resurrected upon disbelief and enmity toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. We ask Allah for forgiveness.
Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad narrated to me from his father, who said:
The Abyssinians gathered and said to al-Najāshī: You have abandoned our religion.
They rose in revolt against him, so he sent for Jaʿfar and his companions, prepared ships for them, and said:
Embark; if I am defeated, go on your way, and if I am victorious, stay.
Then he took a sheet and wrote on it:
He bears witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muḥammad is His servant and messenger, and he bears witness that Jesus is His servant, His messenger, His spirit and His word, which He cast into Mary.
Then he put it inside his cloak and went out to the Abyssinians, who lined up before him, and he said:
O people of Abyssinia! Am I not the one with the most right over you of all people?
They said: Indeed.
He said: Then how have you found my conduct among you?
They said: The best of conduct.
He said: Then what is the matter with you?
They said: You have abandoned our religion and claimed that Jesus is a servant.
He said: Then what do you say about him?
They said: He is the son of Allah.
He said, placing his hand on his chest over his cloak: He bears witness that Jesus was no more than this.
He meant only what he had written. So they were satisfied and went away.
That reached the Prophet ﷺ, and when al-Najāshī died he prayed over him and asked forgiveness ⟦1:440⟧ for him (1) .
Among the merits of al-Najāshī: Umm Ḥabībah Ramlah bint Abī Sufyān ibn Ḥarb al-Umawiyyah, the Mother of the Believers, embraced Islam early on with her husband ʿUbayd (2) Allāh ibn Jaḥsh al-Asadī. Her husband emigrated with her, slipping away with her to the land of Abyssinia, and she bore him Ḥabībah, the stepdaughter of the Prophet ﷺ.
Then wretchedness overtook him: the Christian religion pleased him and he became a Christian, and it was not long (3) before he died in Abyssinia.
When her waiting period was completed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent to propose to her, and she accepted. al-Najāshī took the matter in hand, witnessed her marriage to the Prophet ﷺ, and gave her the dower on behalf of the Prophet ﷺ from his own wealth, four hundred dinars. Thus she obtained something that none of the other Mothers of the Believers obtained. Then al-Najāshī prepared her trousseau (4) .
The one who went to al-Najāshī with the proposal for her was ʿAmr ibn Umayyah al-Ḍamrī, according to what al-Wāqidī transmitted with a mursal (مرسل) chain of transmission (الإسناد).
Then he said: Muḥammad ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to me from ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUmar ibn Qatādah.
And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to me from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr; the two of them said:
The one who gave her in marriage, and to whom al-Najāshī made the proposal, was Khālid ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ al-Umawī. Her age when she came to Medina was thirty-odd years (5) .
معمر: عن الزهري، عن عروة، عن أم حبيبة: 
that she had been married to ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh, who had travelled to al-Najāshī, and that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her in Abyssinia; ⟦1:441⟧ al-Najāshī gave her to him in marriage, gave her a dower of four thousand dirhams from his own wealth, and sent her with Shuraḥbīl ibn Ḥasanah, and all her trousseau was from al-Najāshī (1) .
As for Ibn Lahīʿah, he transmitted: عن أبي الأسود، عن عروة، قال: 
ʿUthmān (may Allah be pleased with him) married her to him in Abyssinia.
This is an error, for ʿUthmān was in Medina with the Prophet ﷺ, and he was never absent from him except on the day of Badr, when the Prophet ﷺ ordered him to stay behind to nurse his wife, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Ibn Saʿd said: أنبأنا محمد بن عمر، أنبأنا عبد الله بن عمرو بن زهير، عن إسماعيل بن عمرو بن سعيد بن العاص، قال: 
Umm Ḥabībah said: I saw in a dream as though ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh were in the worst and most deformed of forms, and I was alarmed. Then, when morning came, he said:
O Umm Ḥabībah! I have looked into religion and have not seen a religion better than Christianity. I had professed it, then entered the religion of Muḥammad, and now I have returned to it.
I told him of the dream, but he paid no heed to it, and he gave himself over to wine until he died.
Then I saw in a dream as though someone came and said to me: O Mother of the Believers! I was alarmed, and I interpreted it to mean that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would marry me.
No sooner had my waiting period ended than, before I knew it, al-Najāshī's messenger was at my door asking leave. It was a slave girl of his called al-Barhah, who looked after his clothes and his oil. She came in to me and said:
The king says to you: The Messenger of Allah has written to me to give you to him in marriage.
I said: May Allah give you good tidings.
She said: The king says: Appoint someone to give you in marriage.
So she sent to Khālid ibn Saʿīd and appointed him as her agent, and she gave al-Barhah two silver bracelets, rings that were on her toes, and two anklets that were on her legs.
When it was evening, al-Najāshī ordered Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib and the Muslims who were there to come, and they attended.
al-Najāshī delivered the marriage address, saying: Praise be ⟦1:442⟧ to Allah, the King, the Holy, the Peace. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muḥammad is His servant and messenger, and that he is the one whose coming Jesus ﷺ foretold.
Then Khālid ibn Saʿīd delivered an address and gave her in marriage, and he received the four hundred dinars. Then he called for food, and they ate.
She said: When the money reached me, I set aside fifty dinars for al-Barhah, but she refused, and she brought out a casket containing everything I had given her, returned it, and said:
The king has firmly charged me not to take anything from you. I have submitted to Allah, and what I ask of you is that you convey my greetings of peace to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Then she brought me, from the king's women, aloeswood, ambergris and much civet (1) .
It has been said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ consummated the marriage with her in the year 6.
Khalīfah said: He consummated the marriage with her in the year 7 of the Hijrah.
Aṣḥamah in Arabic means: gift.
When he died, the Prophet ﷺ said to the people: (A brother of yours has died in the land of Abyssinia) .
He went out with them to the open ground, arranged them in rows, then prayed over him (2) .
Some scholars have transmitted that this was in the month of Rajab, in the year 9 of the Hijrah.
